title: UGC Agency vs AI UGC Agency for Meta Ads: How to Choose
summary: Real creators or AI presenters? Compare UGC and AI UGC agencies for Meta ads on cost, partnership ads, AI labels and who runs the ads, as of October 2026.
body_markdown:
Hire a real-creator UGC agency when the ad needs a real person's experience, or a partnership ad that runs from a creator's own handle. Hire an AI UGC agency when you need many scripted variations at a steady pace and can accept AI presenters. Knowlify is our top pick for the AI route, with about 25 finished ads a week and optional Meta campaign management, and we do not supply real creators. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## What separates the two models?


A real-creator agency sources people, briefs them, and manages filming, usage rights and payments. The output is footage of a real person who can post the content, and in some cases the ad can run from that creator's handle.


An AI UGC agency produces scripted ads with AI presenters, finished with editing and quality review.[Admiral Media's AI UGC page](https://admiral.media/ai-ugc-agency/) says its AI UGC is scripted advertising, not content submitted by a real customer. That distinction matters most when the ad makes a personal claim. Our[AI UGC versus creator UGC cost guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-ugc-vs-creator-ugc-cost) covers the numbers behind each route.


As of October 2026, the[FTC's testimonials rule questions and answers](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) say there is no blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing. An avatar is prohibited, however, when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false. Write the claim first, then choose the model that can support it.


Meta treats the formats differently too. Its[partnership ads documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/ad-creative/partnership-ads) describes running Facebook and Instagram ads from a creator's or partner's handle. An AI presenter generated for your ads has no handle of its own, so those ads need a real creator.

## Knowlify: our top pick for AI UGC on Meta


Knowlify fits the AI route because it is set up for a weekly testing rhythm: about 25 finished ads a week, a first batch on day 5, and a person checking every ad before delivery. Our[AI UGC service](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) makes UGC-style ads with AI presenters talking to camera, and the team also makes 3D and character animation and AI commercials. That cadence suits a team that needs new hooks each week, and the AI route is strongest when the test is about angles, hooks and offers rather than a person's experience.


You can add end-to-end Meta campaign management, or take creative only if you already have a buyer. Pricing is a custom quote. Where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. On creative-only plans, if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the site, linked from our[pricing and guarantee section](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ).


Compare prices by finished, approved ad. Admiral Media's Starter batch is €10,000 for 20 ads, and its page says its ideal clients invest US$50,000 or more a month in paid media. Brighter Click's 12 edited creator videos cost $4,500. The units differ, so divide each quote by the approved ads it buys before you compare.


**When to pick another option:** choose a real-creator agency for a real customer's experience or a partnership ad from a creator's handle. Knowlify does not supply real human creators or post from creator accounts.


## What do real creators add that AI cannot?


Real creators bring permissions you must manage. Get written usage rights for each creator, including the territories and the length of the rights. Brighter Click lists full usage rights in perpetuity on its package, and Insense lists full digital usage rights across channels, so compare the exact scope in each contract.


Creator relationships also need care in the ad itself. The FTC's[endorsement guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking) explains why an advertising message should not misrepresent a speaker's experience. That is why an AI presenter should never claim to have used the product, and why a real creator should describe only what they actually did.
